+# SWA ERP — Architecture Overview (for the server / app-dev team)
+
+*Forward this as-is. It answers the questions raised in the 24 Jun meeting: hosting, database, and what "the APIs" actually are.*
+
+---
+
+## 1. What this application is
+
+A single internal web application (ERP) for SWA. One backend, one database, one web frontend. Users reach it in a browser over the office VPN. No external/paid third-party APIs are involved.
+
+## 2. Deployment target (as discussed)
+
+- **On-prem Windows Server**, 128 GB RAM (extendable), currently used as file storage + RDP. IT confirmed it handles 100+ users.
+- Access: users connect over **VPN**, then open the app in a browser (a desktop shortcut to the internal URL, e.g. `http://swa-erp.local` or `http://<server-ip>`).
+- This app is light: a web server + an app server + one database. It will sit comfortably alongside the existing file-storage role.
+
+## 3. The three parts (all on the same server)
+
+```
+[ User's browser over VPN ]
+            │  HTTP (internal network only)
+            ▼
+[ Web frontend ]  React static files, served by the web server
+            │  REST calls on the same server  (these are the "APIs")
+            ▼
+[ App backend ]   Python (FastAPI) — business logic, auth, validation
+            │  SQL on localhost
+            ▼
+[ Database ]      ONE PostgreSQL instance — the single master database
+```
+
+## 4. Clearing up two points from the meeting
+
+- **"Are the APIs paid / external?"** — No. "API" here just means the internal REST endpoints our own frontend calls on our own backend, on the same server. Nothing leaves the network. No subscriptions.
+- **"Is there a master database, or separate databases?"** — There is **one master PostgreSQL database**. All modules (clients, inquiries, agreements, tokens, projects, documents, time logs, sustainability) are tables inside that one database, with proper foreign keys. We are *not* splitting data across multiple databases. (A single database is easier to back up, keeps relationships intact, and is the standard choice at this scale. If something needs isolation later, Postgres handles that with schemas — still one server.)
+
+## 5. Software to install on the Windows Server
+
+Two equivalent options — the server team picks based on their comfort:
+
+**Option A — Docker (recommended, simplest to operate)**
+- Install **Docker Desktop for Windows** (uses WSL2).
+- We ship a `docker-compose.yml`: it brings up backend + frontend + PostgreSQL + Redis in one command. Updates = pull new image, restart.
+
+**Option B — Native Windows services**
+- **PostgreSQL for Windows** (installer, runs as a Windows service).
+- **Python 3.11** + our backend, run as a service (e.g. via NSSM) behind **IIS** or **nginx** for Windows serving the React files.
+
+Either way: open one internal port (e.g. 80/443) on the LAN; no public internet exposure.
+
+## 6. Resource footprint (estimate)
+
+- Idle: ~1–2 GB RAM. Under 100 concurrent users: well under 8 GB. Negligible vs the 128 GB available.
+- Disk: the database is small (tens of MB of rows). Uploaded documents (DRN files) grow with usage — point them at the existing file-storage volume.
+
+## 7. Backups
+
+- One nightly `pg_dump` of the single database → onto the existing file-storage backup routine. That's the whole backup story. Document files back up with the file server as they already do.
+
+## 8. What we need from the server team
+
+1. Confirm OS (Windows Server — version?) and whether Docker Desktop/WSL2 is allowed.
+2. An internal hostname/IP + one LAN port for the app.
+3. A folder on the file-storage volume for uploaded documents.
+4. 15 min on a call to agree on Option A vs B.

+# SWA ERP — Scope & Data Model (v1, derived from source)
+
+**Source of truth:** the 20 Excel sheets in `resourses/ERP Sheets/` + the recorded meeting (24 Jun 2026).
+This document is what the client could not hand us as a written problem statement. We derived it ourselves from their data and their words. Every field below is copied from an actual sheet header — nothing invented.
+
+---
+
+## 1. The one rule that decides scope: interconnected vs independent
+
+The client was explicit: **build the interconnected chain first. Ignore the independent chains for the first build.**
+
+### IN SCOPE — the interconnected chain (first build, 8 modules)
+
+```
+INQUIRY ──converts?──► CLIENT (exists? reuse : create) ──► PROJECT
+                                                             │
+                  SERVICE AGREEMENT (yearly) ──► TOKEN ──────┤  (billing track, limited clients)
+                                                             │
+                              per project, per employee ─────┼──► DRN  (document referencing)
+                                                             ├──► TIME LOG
+                                                             │
+                              after project completes ───────┴──► SUSTAINABILITY METRICS
+```
+
+Note: **DRN and Time Log also occur OUTSIDE a project** (for Marketing and R&D work). Their link field is therefore polymorphic — it can point to a Project, a Token, or a Document. (See §3.7.)
+
+### OUT OF SCOPE for first build (defer or drop)
+
+| Item | Decision | Reason (from meeting) |
+|---|---|---|
+| **BOQ / Quotation (current Wave 3)** | **DROP from ERP** | Client: "we do not have any space for BOQ or quotation in ERP." This came from the rfq2boq product, which is **separate**. It was copied into our problem statement by mistake. |
+| Client Complaints | Defer | "we can also not have in the first build" |
+| Client Satisfaction / Feedback | Defer | same |
+| Marketing (Instagram / LinkedIn / Website) | Defer (independent) | independent chain |
+| R&D (Collaborations / Innovations) | Defer (independent) | independent chain |
+| HR independent sheets (Employees, Training, Hardware, Admin Process, Emp Feedback) | Defer (independent) | independent chain; keep models, no UI |
+
+**Result: first build = 8 modules.** Inquiries, Clients, Service Agreements, Tokens, Projects, DRN, Time Logging, Sustainability.
+Backend for all 8 already exists (wave-9). What's missing: frontend pages + Excel data migration + the last test fixes.
+
+---
+
+## 2. The business flow, exactly as the client described it
+
+1. An **Inquiry** enters the system first.
+2. If the inquiry **converts**:
+   - Check the **Client** database. If the client **exists** → go straight to **Project**. If it **does not exist** → create the **Client** first, then the **Project**.
+   - The inquiry becomes a project.
+3. For a **Project**, employees do **Document Referencing (DRN)** and **Time Logging**.
+   - DRN and Time Logging also happen **outside** a project (Marketing, R&D).
+4. After a **Project** completes → record **Sustainability Metrics** (the impact created).
+5. **Service Agreement + Token** track (parallel, for a limited set of clients):
+   - We sign a **Service Agreement for an entire year** — not project-by-project, a full-year engagement.
+   - A **Token** is the applicable billable unit under that agreement.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Data model — real fields from each sheet
+
+> ID convention seen in real data: `SWA-{YEAR}-{TYPE}-{NNN}`.
+> ⚠️ Discrepancy to confirm: Clients are `SWA-2025-CL-001` in the sheets (TYPE = **CL**), but our code uses **CLT**. Pick one. Recommend matching the sheets (**CL**) so migrated IDs are stable. DRN uses a continuous serial, not year-scoped.
+
+### 3.1 Inquiries — `Inquiries Sheet.xlsx` (37 real rows)
+`Sr No · Inquiry ID · Inquiry Date · Inquiry Type · Inquiry Source · Client Name · Requirement Summary · Estimated Value · Priority · Status · Owner · Technical Lead · Notes`
+- IDs: `SWA-2025-INQ-001…`  · Status: `Converted` / blank · Type: `Design` · Priority: `High`…
+
+### 3.2 Clients — `Clients Sheet.xlsx` (header row 2; data to be filled)
+`Sr No · Client ID · Client Name · Industry · Date Onboarded · Primary Contact · Email · Phone · Billing Address · Client Status · First Lead ID · First Inquiry ID · Notes`
+
+### 3.3 Service Agreements — `Service Agreements Sheet.xlsx` (real rows)
+`Sr No · Agreement ID · Client Name · Client ID · Inquiry ID · Service Name · Start Date · End Date · Total Tokens · Status · Notes`
+- e.g. `SWA-2025-SA-011 · ABCD · SWA-2025-CL-001 · SWA-2025-INQ-001 · INSUDESIGN · 2025-10-01 → 2026-03-31 · Active · Monthly Billing`
+- `Total Tokens` can be `N/A`. Status: `Active`.
+
+### 3.4 Tokens — `Tokens Sheet.xlsx` (**252 rows — the big migration**)
+`Sr No · Date · Token ID · Agreement ID · Token Type · Description · Token Status · Tokens Used · SWA Employee Name · Client Employee Name`
+- Token Status: `In Progress` / `Closed`.
+
+### 3.5 Project Tracking — `Project Tracking Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Project ID · Client ID · Inquiry ID · Client Name · Project Name · Start date · End date · Milestone · Progress Indicators · Status Updates · Team Leader · Project owner`
+
+### 3.6 DRN (Document Reference) — `Document Reference Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · DRN · Associated Project ID · Author · Document Type · Type · User · Description · Revision · Status · Remarks`
+- **DRN** = unique document number (primary key). Three-letter doc codes: **CON / DBR** (Design Basis Report), **GAD/GED** (General Assembly Drawing). Continuous serial.
+- `Associated Project ID` = FK to Project. `Type` = Submittal / Internal / Revision. `User` = Client / Reviewer / Authority (low value — candidate to drop, no downstream dependency). `Revision` = R0, R1… `Status` = approval state.
+
+### 3.7 Time Logging — `Time Logging Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · Employee Name · Employee Role · Work Type · Reference ID · Revision · Project Name · Activity Type · Software Used · Work Mode · Hours Logged · Billable Hours`
+- **`Reference ID` is polymorphic** — "primary linkage with project OR token OR doc."
+- **`Hours Logged` is in 0.5h intervals** (the sheet says so — *not* 15-min; update CLAUDE.md). `Work Mode` = Manual / Automatic. `Software Used` = dropdown (except Microsoft Office).
+
+### 3.8 Sustainability Metrics — `Sustainability Metrics Sheet.xlsx`
+`Sr No · Date · Reference ID · Compliant with Green Standards · Total Energy Saved (kWh) · CO2 emissions avoided (tCO2e) · Lifecycle Cost savings delivered (INR) · Insulation Efficiency (Actual/Expected) · Payback Period (Months)`
+- `Reference ID` links to a Project (`SWA-2025-PRJ-065`). Green standards: `No` / `GRIHA` / etc.
+
+---
+
+## 4. What's left to ship the first build
+
+| Layer | State | Owner |
+|---|---|---|
+| Backend models + API for 8 modules | ✅ exists (wave-9), ~23 tests red | running test-fix agents |
+| Frontend pages for 6 of 8 (Clients + Projects already exist) | ❌ 0 built | new OpenCode window(s) — see `work/wave-10/` |
+| Excel → DB migration (252 tokens etc.) | ❌ not written | new OpenCode window — see `work/wave-10/` |
+| Remove BOQ/Quotation from ERP nav/scope | ❌ still present (Wave 3) | follow-up |
+
+---
+
+## 5. Open items to raise with the client (specific, not "give me everything")
+
+1. **Client ID code:** sheets use `CL`, our code uses `CLT`. Confirm canonical → we standardize migration.
+2. **DRN `User` and `Document Type` columns** have no downstream dependency — keep or drop? (We recommend keep as free-text category, drop nothing destructive.)
+3. **Service Agreement `Total Tokens` = N/A** in some rows — unlimited, or unknown? Affects token-cap logic.
+4. **Time Log `Reference ID`** points to project/token/doc — confirm all three are real linkages we must support (we're building it polymorphic).
+5. Server-team call: confirm Windows Server, single PostgreSQL service, app reached over VPN via shortcut. (See `ARCHITECTURE_FOR_SERVER_TEAM.md`.)

 """Business-ID generator.
 
 Produces IDs like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`. Uses a DB-backed sequence counter
 (`IdSequence`) so each (type_code, year) pair advances atomically.
 
 Pass `year=0` for "continuous across years" (per meeting: DBR/CAS/GAD numbers
 do not reset per year).
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from datetime import datetime
 
 from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
 
 from src.backend.models.id_sequence import IdSequence
 
 
 def current_year() -> int:
     return datetime.utcnow().year
 
 
 def next_business_id(db: Session, type_code: str, year: int | None = None) -> str:
     """Generate the next business ID for `type_code`.
 
     Args:
         db: SQLAlchemy session.
         type_code: Short code like `CLT`, `INQ`, `SA`, `TKN`, `PRJ`, `EMP`,
             `FDB`, `TRN`, `HW`, `PROC`, `COL`, `INN`, `FB`, `CMP`,
             `IG`, `LI`, `WEB`, `CON`, `DBR`, `CAS`, `GAD`, `KDR`, `RDP`,
             `VAL`, `RPT`, `OTH`.
         year: Calendar year (defaults to current year). Pass `0` for
             continuous counters (e.g. DBR numbers per the meeting transcript).
 
     Returns:
         A formatted ID string like `SWA-2025-CLT-001`.
     """
     if year is None:
         year = current_year()
 
     seq = (
         db.query(IdSequence)
         .filter_by(type_code=type_code, year=year)
         .with_for_update()
         .one_or_none()
     )
     if seq is None:
         seq = IdSequence(type_code=type_code, year=year, last_value=0)
         db.add(seq)
         db.flush()
 
     seq.last_value += 1
     db.flush()

+# Task B — Excel → DB migration script
+
+**You own `scripts/migrate_excel.py` (new file). Do not touch `src/frontend` or `tests`. Read-only on the Excel files.**
+
+## Goal
+Import the real data from `resourses/ERP Sheets/*.xlsx` into the PostgreSQL database, in dependency order, idempotently, with a dry-run mode. First build = the 8 interconnected modules only.
+
+## Source data quirks (read `SCOPE_AND_DATA_MODEL.md` §3 first)
+- Header row is **not** always row 1. Several sheets have a blank row 0 and headers on row 1 or 2, plus a "meaning/why" annotation row underneath. Detect the header row by finding the row containing known labels (e.g. "Inquiry ID", "Token ID").
+- ID code mismatch: sheets use `SWA-2025-CL-001` (CL) for clients; code uses CLT. **Preserve the sheet's business IDs** on import (store as the business_id) so foreign keys across sheets resolve. Flag the discrepancy in the report; do not silently rewrite.
+- `Tokens Sheet.xlsx` has **252 rows** — the main load. `Service Agreements` Total Tokens can be `N/A`. Time Log hours are 0.5h intervals. Sustainability/TimeLog/DRN use a `Reference ID` that may point to a Project, Token, or Document.
+
+## Import order (respect FKs)
+1. Inquiries → 2. Clients → 3. Service Agreements → 4. Tokens → 5. Projects → 6. DRN → 7. Time Logs → 8. Sustainability.
+Resolve cross-sheet references by business ID (e.g. token.agreement_id → the agreement row's Agreement ID).
+
+## Interface
+```
+python scripts/migrate_excel.py --dry-run     # parse + validate + print per-sheet row counts and any unresolved FKs; writes nothing
+python scripts/migrate_excel.py --commit       # insert into DB; idempotent (skip rows whose business_id already exists)
+python scripts/migrate_excel.py --only tokens  # optional: one module
+```
+- Use the existing SQLAlchemy models/session (`src/backend/db/session.py`, `src/backend/models`). Do not hand-write SQL.
+- Idempotent: re-running `--commit` must not duplicate rows.
+- Never modify the Excel files.
+
+## Done when
+- `--dry-run` prints a clean table: sheet → rows parsed → rows that would insert → unresolved references (ideally 0), exit code 0.
+- `--commit` loads the 8 modules; afterwards `python scripts/demo_live_api.py` lists real migrated rows (e.g. 252 tokens).

def list_time_logs_service(
    db: Session,
    page: int = 1,
    page_size: int = 20,
    q: str | None = None,
    employee_id: str | None = None,
    work_type: str | None = None,
    start_date: date | None = None,
    end_date: date | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[TimeLog], int, int, int]:
    items, total = list_time_logs(
        db, page, page_size, q, employee_id, work_type, start_date, end_date

    return items, total, page, page_size


def create_time_log_service(db: Session, data: TimeLogCreate, actor_id: uuid.UUID | None) -> TimeLog:
    time_log = create_time_log(db, data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))

        db,
        action="time_log.create",
        entity_type="time_log",
        entity_id=time_log.id,
        user_id=actor_id,
        after_json={
            "id": str(time_log.id),
            "log_date": time_log.log_date.isoformat(),
            "employee_id": str(time_log.employee_id),

    before_json = {
        "log_date": time_log.log_date.isoformat(),
        "employee_id": str(time_log.employee_id),

        "reference_id": time_log.reference_id,

def delete_time_log_service(
    db: Session,
    time_log_id: uuid.UUID,

) -> bool:
    time_log = get_by_id(db, time_log_id)

    before_json = {

        "billable_hours": float(time_log.billable_hours),
        "remarks": time_log.remarks,
    }

    create_entry(
        db,
        action="time_log.delete",
        entity_type="time_log",
        entity_id=time_log.id,
        user_id=actor_id,
        before_json=before_json,
        after_json=after_json,
    )

    return True


def aggregate_time_logs_service(
    db: Session,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    employee_id: Optional[uuid.UUID] = None,
    work_type: Optional[str] = None,
    start_date: Optional[date] = None,
    end_date: Optional[date] = None,
) -> dict:
    from sqlalchemy import func, and_
    from src.backend.models.time_log import TimeLog

    query = db.query(
        func.sum(TimeLog.hours_logged).label("total_hours"),
        func.sum(TimeLog.billable_hours).label("total_billable_hours"),
    )

    if project_id:
        query = query.filter(TimeLog.reference_id == str(project_id))
    if employee_id:
        query = query.filter(TimeLog.employee_id == employee_id)
    if work_type:
        query = query.filter(TimeLog.work_type == work_type)
    if start_date:
        query = query.filter(TimeLog.log_date >= start_date)
    if end_date:
        query = query.filter(TimeLog.log_date <= end_date)

    result = query.first()

    return {
        "total_hours": float(result.total_hours or 0),
        "total_billable_hours": float(result.total_billable_hours or 0),
    }
